Class SlotGroupCategories

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.slot.SlotGroupCategories
public final class SlotGroupCategories extends Object
Library-owned registry of per-menu-class SlotGroupResolvers. Parallel to MenuChrome in shape, exact-class-only resolution, first-registration-wins for the primary resolver, library-shipped providers for vanilla classes, modded consumers register for their own classes via register(Class, SlotGroupResolver).

Consumers registering into a vanilla menu (M4 slot-injection pattern) and wanting their registered slot group to participate in SlotGroupContext dispatch declare their category via extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver), additive, collision-rejecting, preserves the library's first-wins guarantee for register.

See Design Docs/Phase 12.5/M8_FOUR_CONTEXT_MODEL.md §5.3 for the resolver design and §6 for the full vanilla coverage catalog. See Design Docs/Phase 12.5/V5_7_EXTEND_RESOLVER_FIX.md for the extend design note + collision policy.

Resolution, exact-class only

of(AbstractContainerMenu) looks up by menu.getClass(). no inheritance walk. Rationale matches MenuChrome: vanilla subclass relationships don't reliably predict slot-layout relationships (e.g. CraftingMenu extends AbstractCraftingMenu which extends RecipeBookMenu, but each concrete menu has its own slot ordering). Modded consumers register for their own concrete menu classes.

Created slots publish here too

Every MenuKit-Containers slot group declares a SlotGroupCategory on its spec, and Containers registers one universal resolver (extendEvery(CreatedGroupResolver)) that reports those groups on whatever menu they sit. So of(AbstractContainerMenu) and categoriesBySlot(AbstractContainerMenu) name created and vanilla slots alike, with nothing but MK types, the registry is the kind-blind way for one mod to find another's slots.

Primary vs. extensions

Each class has at most one primary resolver (from register(Class, SlotGroupResolver)) and zero or more extension resolvers (from extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver)). of(AbstractContainerMenu) runs the primary first, then each extension in registration order, merging outputs. Extensions can only ADD new categories, an extension emitting a category the primary (or an earlier extension) already emitted is dropped with a warn log. This preserves library-defined category meaning across the mod ecosystem.

    • register

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu> void register(Class<T> menuClass, SlotGroupResolver resolver)

    • extend

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu> void extend(Class<T> menuClass, SlotGroupResolver resolver)
      Registers an additional resolver for a menu class, contributing extra categories without replacing the primary. Multiple extensions per class are allowed, applied in registration order.

      Use case. A consumer slots a slot into a vanilla menu (e.g. FurnaceMenu) via M4 slot-injection and wants their registered slot group to participate in SlotGroupContext dispatch under a consumer-owned category. The library's primary resolver for the vanilla menu is already registered and first-wins blocks a replacement; extend is the additive path.

      Collision policy, additive only, no redefinition. If this extension emits a SlotGroupCategory that the primary resolver or an earlier extension already emitted for the same class, the duplicate entry is dropped at resolve time with a warn log. Earlier entry wins. This preserves library-defined category meaning (e.g. FURNACE_INPUT means one slot list, consistent across mods) and matches the first-wins-with-warn pattern of register(Class, SlotGroupResolver).

      The class does not need a primary registered first, extensions can stand alone.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the menu type
      Parameters:
      menuClass - the concrete menu class
      resolver - the extension resolver

    • extendEvery

      @Internal public static void extendEvery(com.trevlar.menukit.inject.CreatedGroupResolver resolver)
      Registers a resolver that runs on every menu, after the class-specific primary and extensions. Its categories merge: one the menu already resolved gains the resolver's slots appended after the existing ones; a new category is added. This is how created slots (MenuKit-Containers) publish their groups. they sit on whatever menu the player opened, so no menu class names them. Each contribution becomes its own ResolvedSlotGroup, never folded into the category it declares, several created groups can share one category and they do not share a bounding box. Library-internal seat; consumers declare a created group's category on its SlotSpec and never call this.

    • declare

      public static void declare(SlotGroupCategory category)
      Publishes category to the registry so another mod can find it through all() without a menu open. Idempotent.

      MenuKit declares its own vanilla constants at init, and MenuKit-Containers declares a created group's category when the group registers, so a consumer that mints a category only calls this when it wants the category listed before anything is registered against it.

    • all

      public static List<SlotGroupCategory> all()
      Every category the registry knows: MenuKit's vanilla constants, every category a created slot group declared, and anything a mod declare(SlotGroupCategory)d. Sorted by namespace then path so the listing is stable.

      This is the discovery half of the registry, "what kinds of slot exist?". and it needs no open menu. The other half is per-menu: of(AbstractContainerMenu) for the slots in each category right now, categoriesBySlot(AbstractContainerMenu) for the inverse.

    • categoriesBySlot

      public static Map<net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot, SlotGroupCategory> categoriesBySlot(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      The category of each slot on menu, by slot identity, the inverse of of(AbstractContainerMenu), for a consumer walking menu.slots and asking "what is this one?" A slot in no category is absent. Kind-blind: a vanilla slot and a created slot answer the same way, so a consumer can decide per category ("search PLAYER_INVENTORY and this mod's pockets; leave its elytra slot alone") without knowing which library put a slot there.

    • groups

      public static List<ResolvedSlotGroup> groups(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      Every slot group on menu, each with its own identity and its own slots, the ANCHOR view, the one with geometry in it. A panel anchors to one of these; a group has a bounding box and a category does not.

      Resolution order: the primary resolver for menu.getClass() (if any), then each extension in registration order, then every universal resolver (extendEvery(CreatedGroupResolver)). Each vanilla category yields one group; an extension category that collides with an already-claimed one is dropped with a warn log per extend(Class, SlotGroupResolver)'s policy. Each created contribution yields its own group.

      Empty for menus where nothing resolves.

    • of

      public static Map<SlotGroupCategory, List<net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot>> of(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      Every category on menu with its slots, the SEARCH view, which unions a category's groups because "find me every inventory slot" wants the union. Vanilla slots first, created ones appended, never listed twice.

      For geometry use groups(AbstractContainerMenu) instead: a category's union spans scattered rectangles, so its bounding box means nothing.
